welcome.title: Welcome to Fri3d-IDE
welcome.subtitle: MicroPython IDE for the Fri3d Camp 2026 badge.
welcome.tours-text: Step-by-step tours that walk you through the IDE.
welcome.or-connect: Or skip the tours and connect directly:

onboarding.continue-on-action: Complete the highlighted action to continue
onboarding.welcome-title: What do you want to do?
onboarding.welcome-text: Choose what you want to do.
onboarding.task-welcome-title: What do you want to do?
onboarding.task-welcome-text: Choose what you want to do.
onboarding.task-connect-detail: Use USB to connect a physical Fri3d badge.
onboarding.task-build-detail: Create an app with a step-by-step coding guide beside the editor.
onboarding.task-badgehub-detail: Browse and install a compatible badge app.
onboarding.target-badgehub-title: Where should the app be installed?
onboarding.target-text: Choose a physical Fri3d badge or the virtual badge.
onboarding.target-real-detail: Connect over USB and use the physical badge.
onboarding.target-virtual-detail: Run it in the browser without hardware.
onboarding.connecting-wait: Complete any browser permission prompt to continue.
onboarding.create-first-text: Click Create New App. The guide continues as soon as the dialog opens.
onboarding.configure-app-text: Keep Hello World selected, enter an App ID and display name, then click Create. The coding guide opens automatically.
onboarding.badgehub-text: Click Browse BadgeHub. The guide continues as soon as the store opens.
onboarding.browse-badgehub-text: Search or browse for an app, then click Install. The tour continues after installation.
onboarding.success-connect: Your physical badge is ready for files, apps, and the terminal.
onboarding.success-virtual: You can now experiment without changing a physical badge.
onboarding.success-build: You created an app and opened its code. Keep experimenting, then launch it from Apps.
onboarding.success-badgehub: Installed apps appear in the Apps list and can be launched from there.

connection.title: You are connected
connection.text: This shows your connection status: the badge name and a blinking activity dot. Disconnect here; reconnect any time with the Connect button that appears in its place.

apps.title: Your apps
apps.text: The Apps tab lists every app installed on the badge. Click an app to open its details — and “Create New App” scaffolds a fresh one from a template.

open-app.title: Inside an app
open-app.text: Opening an app shows its files. Click any file to open it in the editor — that’s all it takes to start editing.

launch.title: Launch the app
launch.text: The 🚀 Launch app button starts the app on the badge, exactly like picking it from the badge menu.

launch-toolbar.title: Launch while editing
launch-toolbar.text: When you are editing a file that belongs to an app, this Launch app button appears in the toolbar — so you can start the app right from the editor.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.text: All output from your badge appears here. It is also a live MicroPython REPL: click it and type Python directly on the device.

files.title: File browser — plain MicroPython
files.text: Prefer working without the app structure? The File Manager shows every file on the badge. Open any .py file and run it directly — regular MicroPython, no packaging needed.

save-run.title: Save & Run safely
save-run.text: Use Save & Run to write your changes to badge storage and execute them. The separate Save (Ctrl/Cmd+S) and Run (F5) commands remain available; Run alone does not save changes.

done.title: You're all set! 🚀
done.text: That was the tour! Your badge is connected and ready. Start building amazing things. Happy coding!
done.text-demo: That was the tour! The demo device will now disconnect — plug in your Fri3d badge with a USB-C cable and start building. Happy coding!

first-app-guide.title: Build your first app

virtual-controls.title: Keep the virtual badge out of your way
virtual-controls.move: Move it by dragging the purple handle.
virtual-controls.popout: Click ⧉ to open it in a separate window.
virtual-controls.minimize: Click ▾ to minimize it to the handle. Running a checkpoint restores it automatically.

first-app-guide.check-success: Code looks good. App was saved and launched—check it on your badge.

start.title: Run the starter app
start.instruction: Your new main.py is open in the editor on the right. Start by checking the untouched app and seeing it run.
start.goal: A centered Hello World message appears on the badge.

greeting.title: Make the greeting yours
greeting.instruction: Change the text inside label.set_text. Replace label.center() with the alignment line below so there is room for more controls.
greeting.goal: Your own message appears near the top of the screen.

logging.title: Print a message to the terminal
logging.instruction: Add print(...) inside onCreate, above self.setContentView(screen). print is the simplest way to log what your app is doing. The terminal opens below the editor so you can see the message when the app launches.
logging.goal: Launching the app writes App started in the terminal.

button.title: Add a button
button.instruction: Add this code below the label code and above self.setContentView(screen). Indentation must match the other lines in onCreate.
button.goal: A Tap me button appears below your greeting.

counter.title: Make the button work
counter.instruction: Add state and a click handler below the button code. Each tap will update the greeting label.
counter.goal: Tapping the button increases the number on screen.

progress.title: Fill a progress bar with taps
progress.instruction: Keep self.count = 0, then replace the current on_click function and button.add_event_cb line with the code below. The bar uses a 0–10 range and updates after every tap.
progress.goal: Each tap fills one tenth of the bar. After 10 taps, the counter reads 10/10 and the bar is full.

joystick.title: Steer with the joystick
joystick.instruction: Time to turn this into a game! Add this code below the progress bar code and above self.setContentView(screen). It creates a little ship you steer with the badge joystick. On the virtual badge: click the badge screen first, then steer with the arrow keys.
joystick.goal: A small ship appears and flies around when you move the joystick.

game.title: Catch the spark!
game.instruction: The finale: a real game. Replace everything from def on_key down to screen.add_event_cb(on_key, lv.EVENT.KEY, None) with the code below. It hides the tap button (its job is done), drops a spark at a random spot, and teaches on_key one more trick: press the A button (Enter on the virtual badge) while your ship is close to catch the spark. Every catch fills the bar.
game.goal: Catch 10 sparks to fill the bar and win the game.

errors.wrong-file: Open main.py from the app you created before checking this step.
errors.starter-missing: Starter label is missing. Restore the Hello World template code first.
errors.greeting-unchanged: Change the greeting and move the label upward with label.align(...).
errors.logging-missing: Add a print(...) call so the app writes a message to the terminal.
errors.button-missing: No complete button found yet. Add both lv.button and its label.
errors.counter-missing: Connect the button click to a counter using add_event_cb.
errors.progress-missing: Connect the progress bar to self.count, use a 0–10 range, and stop the counter at 10 taps.
errors.save-failed: Code passed the check, but saving failed. Check the connection and try again.
errors.joystick-missing: No joystick handling found yet. Add on_key, register it with lv.EVENT.KEY, and add the screen to the input group.
errors.game-missing: The game is not finished yet. Add the spark (lv.SYMBOL.CHARGE), move it with random.randint, and catch it with the A button (lv.KEY.ENTER).
